item.title: Chinese peacekeepers to Abyei participate in specialized casualty evacuation training
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
By Huang Hao, Wu Xinwei, and Wei Yongqiang Participants pose for a group photo during the UNISFA specialized casualty evacuation training. BEIJING, Aug. 27 -- The United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) conducted a specialized training program in casualty evacuation from August 24 to 26, 2026. Medical personnel from the 6th Chinese Peacekeeping Military Utility Helicopter Unit to UNISFA and the 3rd Chinese Peacekeeping Quick Reaction Force to UNISFA participated in the training. Alongside personnel from nine peacekeeping units from seven other countries, Chinese peacekeepers took part in the practical exercises and professional exchanges, further strengthening their capabilities in coordinated emergency medical rescue and casualty evacuation across the mission area. Chinese peacekeepers explain standard operating procedures during the UNISFA specialized casualty evacuation training. Chinese peacekeepers work through a simulated scenarioduring the UNISFA specialized casualty evacuation training. Peacekeepers evacuate simulated casualties during the UNISFA specialized casualty evacuation training.

item.title: International Community Needs to See through Japan's Dangerous Agenda: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
BEIJING, Aug. 27 -- The international community needs to see through the dangerous agenda pursued by Japan' s right-wing forces, firmly contain the reckless moves of Japan's "neo-militarism", and resolutely safeguard regional peace and stability, said Senior Colonel Zhang Xiaogang, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense, on Thursday. It is reported that Japan's Ministry of Defense will be largely expanded and establish three new departments in 2027. Japan also plans to equip its unmanned underwater vehicle with long-range missiles. Additionally, Japan reached an agreement with Australia on the test of its hypersonic missile in Australia. When being asked to share comment, the Chinese defense spokesperson first pointed out that Japan, as a defeated country of WWII, is prohibited from obtaining offensive weapons by the Potsdam Proclamation and Japan's pacifist Constitution itself. However, according to the spokesperson, Japan has accelerated its "remilitarization" and openly expanded its military arsenal in recent years. These dangerous moves bear striking resemblance to efforts made by the militarist regime in preparing and launching wars in WWII. "As a warmongering and aggressive power in the past, Japan has never genuinely reflected on its historical crimes. If it were allowed to rearm and become a 'war-capable state', the tragic history may well repeat itself," warned the spokesperson. In the end, he urged the international community to see through the dangerous agenda pursued by Japan’s right-wing forces, firmly contain the reckless moves of Japan's "neo-militarism", and resolutely safeguard regional peace and stability.

item.title: 13th Beijing Xiangshan Forum to Be Held from Sept. 15 to 17: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
BEIJING, Aug. 27 -- The 13th Beijing Xiangshan Forum will be held from September 15 to 17, 2026, at Beijing International Convention Center,said Senior Colonel Zhang Xiaogang, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a regular press briefing on Thursday. Under the theme "Build Consensus on Stability, Advance Security Governance Together", this year's forum will feature four plenary sessions on International Order and Strategic Stability, Localized Conflicts: Predicaments and Pathways to Resolution, Risks and Challenges to Security and Stability in the Asia-Pacific, and The Role and Vision of Developing Countries. In addition, this forum will hold eight parallel sessions including Major-country Relations and Strategic Stability, Asian Approaches to Addressing Security Challenges, Sea Lane Security and Maritime Security Governance, Risks and Regulation of Military Applications of Emerging Technologies, and Trends in Outer Space Security Governance. "The 4th China-Africa Peace and Security Forum will also be convened in conjunction with the Xiangshan Forum," the spokesperson added. According to the spokesperson, the Beijing Xiangshan Forum will celebrate its 20th anniversary this year. Guided by the spirit of equality, openness, inclusiveness and mutual learning, the forum has evolved from a Track 2 exchange among defense think tanks into a major Track 1.5 platform for international security and defense dialogue. It serves to build consensus, deepen trust, and advance cooperation in global security governance and fostering a community with a shared future for humanity. "We invite defense and military leaders, representatives of international organizations, and renowned scholars to join the forum as we mark its 20th anniversary and explore solutions to global security governance together," said the spokesperson.

item.title: Xi to attend SCO summit, pay state visit to Kyrgyzstan, Egypt
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- From August 30 to September 3, Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit 2026 in Bishkek, and pay a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt upon the invitation of President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan and President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi of Egypt, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Wednesday.

item.title: Xi urges all-out rescue, relief efforts after mudslide hits border port in Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out efforts to search and rescue people who are missing after a mudslide in Nepal caused casualties at Gyirong border port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Wednesday morning. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, called for efforts to evacuate residents at risk and provide timely medical treatment to the injured to minimize casualties. He made the instructions after a mudslide occurred at around 10:30 a.m. on Wednesday in Nepal, which caused severe casualties and left people unaccounted for at Gyirong border port in Gyirong County. Xi also stressed the need to strengthen monitoring and early warning, ensure scientific rescue operations and guard against secondary disasters. Noting that China is currently in a critical period of flood control, he urged local authorities and relevant departments to prepare for worst-case scenarios and extreme situations, fully implement measures for flood and typhoon prevention, and step up efforts to identify and address potential risks and hazards. He demanded resolute action to prevent major and catastrophic disasters and accidents and safeguard people's lives and property. Premier Li Qiang also issued instructions, calling for an immediate verification of the number of the missing and affected people and for all-out rescue and relief efforts. Li, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, instructed the Foreign Ministry to strengthen communication and coordination with relevant countries, promptly share information and work together to properly handle rescue and relief efforts. Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing, also a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, led officials from relevant departments to the site to guide rescue and disaster-response operations. Authorities in Xizang have mobilized forces to carry out search and rescue operations. All relevant operations are underway.
